title: Beach and rocks
status: draft 2026-11-23 - controller text, fact-checked; art and tap shapes to follow

things.name: Sand
things.say: Most beach sand is made of tiny bits of a mineral called quartz. Quartz is silicon dioxide, made of silicon and oxygen. Glass is made by melting sand.

box.title: Not all sand is the same
box.say: Some beaches have white sand made of broken shells and coral, which are calcium carbonate. Some beaches near volcanoes have black sand, made from dark volcanic rock.

things.name: Sea water
things.say: Sea water tastes salty because it has salt dissolved in it, mostly sodium chloride. Much of that salt came from rocks on land, carried into the sea by rivers over a very, very long time.

box.title: Where sea salt comes from
box.say: When sea water dries in the sun, the water goes up into the air and the salt stays behind. Some sea salt is made this way, in wide, shallow ponds by the sea.

things.name: Seashell
things.say: A seashell is made mostly of calcium carbonate. Sea animals like snails and clams build their shells using calcium, carbon and oxygen from the sea water.

things.name: Speckled rock
things.say: This speckled rock is granite. It is a mix of minerals you can see as little specks: clear quartz, pink or white feldspar, and shiny black mica. They are made mostly of silicon and oxygen, with some aluminium and potassium.

things.name: Red rock
things.say: Some rocks look red or orange because they have iron oxide in them. Iron oxide is iron joined with oxygen. It is the same chemical as rust.

things.name: Driftwood
things.say: Driftwood is wood that the sea has washed up on the beach. Wood is made mostly of cellulose, which is made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.

things.name: Sea glass
things.say: Sea glass is a piece of old glass that waves and sand have rubbed smooth. Glass is made by melting sand, so it is made mostly of silicon and oxygen too.
